- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) — model tends to be too bullish.
- Underestimate when sentiment is negative or near-zero — model misses downward momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in price (e.g., 70+ → 72+), then fails to sustain or overcorrects.
- Exhibit lag in response to sentiment shifts — model reacts 1–2 days after sentiment changes.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often overcorrects after strong moves, especially in 30-day horizon.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model tends to overpredict peak; when sentiment drops, underpredicts fall.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the first 5–7 days of horizon — adjust downward early if sentiment is weak.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends if sentiment is diverging from price — sentiment may signal reversal.
